title: Fit two new filter cartridges to a half-mask respirator, holding the light mask while each is pushed on and turned
instruction: Fit both new cartridges onto the respirator so that each is locked on, and leave the respirator lying face-down on the bench.
context: Workers who wear reusable half-mask respirators against paint spray, solvent vapours, dust or pesticides (painters, construction laborers, insulation and abatement workers, pesticide handlers) change the cartridges on a schedule: OSHA's respiratory protection standard (29 CFR 1910.134) has the employer implement "a change schedule for canisters and cartridges", and OSHA put the standard's coverage at 5 million respirator wearers. 3M's half-facepiece instructions: "Align cartridge notch with arrow on facepiece, as shown, and push together (Fig. 1). Turn cartridge clockwise to stop (1/4 turn) (Fig. 2)." The figures show the mask held in one hand. The 82 g mask rests on its soft seal with its ports facing up and out; pushing a cartridge on shoves the mask across the bench, and turning it against the squeezed gasket tips the mask over, so one hand holds the mask (by the empty port, then by the fitted cartridge) while the other lines up, pushes and turns.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. Half-mask respirator (3M 6200 half facepiece, grey, 82 g): loose, lying face-down on its seal, chin toward the robot; seal footprint 12 x 10 cm centred at x 21.5, y 0, 8 cm tall. Its two bayonet ports (4.6 cm across, each with a foam gasket and a yellow arrow on the rim) face up and out, 42 degrees from vertical; their centres are at x 21.5, y +5.6 and -5.6, 5 cm up. Head straps lie slack behind it. Two new organic-vapour cartridges (3M 6001, black with a magenta label, 7.5 cm across, 2.5 cm thick, 50 g; a white notch mark on the rim): loose, lying face-up, bayonet down, each on a foam pad (9 x 9 x 1.2 cm, a 4.6 cm square hole in the middle; taped down) at x 11.5, y 13.5 (left) and x 11.5, y -13.5 (right). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: From the poses of the mask and each cartridge, the scorer reads where each cartridge sits on its own port. Per cartridge: 0.2 pushed on (its axis within 8 degrees of the port's, centred within 3 mm, its face on the gasket or squeezing it, which is only possible with the lugs down through the slots); 0.45 instead when also turned clockwise 80 degrees or more from the slot (the stop is at 90: locked). The two add up (0.9 with both locked). 1.0: both locked, the mask lying face-down on the bench (tilted 15 degrees or less, its seal within 5 mm of the bench), every finger 15 mm or more from the mask and the cartridges, and the mask still (under 1 mm in 1 s), held for 1 s. The score is the end state's. On a real mask: each cartridge cannot be pulled off and its notch is a quarter turn clockwise from the arrow; the mask lies on the bench untouched.
reset_notes: Turn each cartridge a quarter turn counter-clockwise, pull it off and lay it face-up on its pad with its notch as in the screenshot; lay the mask face-down in its place. In the simulation each trial starts the simulator afresh (each inspect-robots run does).
fidelity: Rigid bodies in Isaac Sim 6.1 (PhysX), 20 Hz control. The facepiece is one rigid convex shell on its frame (a real one is soft elastomer; its ports are rigid on both). The cartridge is a round disc of the real one's size. The bayonet is modelled: slots, lugs, a lip, stops, a 0.5 mm click pocket; the foam gasket is a compliant contact (10 kN/m per contact patch). The straps are drawn but do not collide.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both grippers reached down beside the cartridges on their pads and toward the mask several times but never took a cartridge; nothing was fitted); demo: 1.0
